shared_elements: central anthropomorphic figure carved in low relief
vertical columns/panels of block-like glyphic or emblem signs
columns flanking the central figure on left and right
elaborated headdress/upper zone above the figure
framed rectangular field on a monolithic upright slab
justification: Both surfaces present the same distinctive scheme of a single frontal/near-frontal anthropomorphic figure in shallow relief occupying a central panel, bracketed on both sides by narrow vertical columns of small block-like sign units, with an elaborated headgear zone toward the top; that combination of central figure plus flanking sign columns is a specific, conventional arrangement rather than a generic one. The main differences are in legibility and detail: A shows a fuller, more articulated body with discernible limbs, costume elements and a second smaller motif in the lower field, while B's central form is reduced to a broad, blocky torso-and-head mass with heavy projecting lateral lugs and far less internal figural detail.
